name: Oxc
summary: The JavaScript Oxidation Compiler: Rust building blocks (parser, transformer, minifier, resolver) under Rolldown and Vite, plus the Oxlint linter and Oxfmt formatter.
intro: Oxc is a set of tools for JavaScript and TypeScript written in Rust (the name plays on oxidation, the process that makes rust). At the bottom are reusable compiler parts: a parser that produces a syntax tree for tooling, a transformer for TypeScript, JSX and newer syntax, a minifier, and a Node-compatible module resolver. They are shared by everything above them, so the linter, formatter and bundler parse code the same way. Rolldown uses them for all its language work, which makes Oxc the compiler inside Vite 8.

Two end-user tools come with it. Oxlint is a linter with more than 870 built-in rules taken from ESLint, typescript-eslint and popular plugins, which the project benchmarks at 50 to 100 times faster than ESLint; its defaults favour rules that catch real bugs. Type-aware rules run through `tsgolint`, built on TypeScript 7 (`tsgo`), and a JavaScript plugin API (alpha) runs existing ESLint plugins. Oxfmt, in beta since February 2026, is a Prettier-compatible formatter that passes all of Prettier’s JavaScript and TypeScript conformance tests and sorts imports and Tailwind classes itself. Vite+ runs both through `vp check`.
strengths: Speed: Shopify’s ESLint run of 75 CI minutes took about 10 seconds with Oxlint on a single worker
Built to replace ESLint and Prettier in place: it reads their configs through migration commands and runs most ESLint plugins unchanged
Type-aware linting covers 59 of typescript-eslint’s 61 type-aware rules and can report TypeScript errors in the same pass
One parser and resolver for linting, formatting, transforming and bundling, so the tools agree on what the code means
limits: Oxfmt is still in beta (pre-1.0) and doesn’t cover every Prettier option or plugin yet
JavaScript plugins are alpha: limited support for Vue, Svelte and Angular file formats, and no custom type-aware rules
Type-aware linting needs a separate `oxlint-tsgolint` package tied to a specific TypeScript version
Minor releases add rules, which can fail CI on code that passed before

story: Boshen Chen wanted to become a full-time Rust developer and joined Rome, a project rewriting JavaScript tooling in Rust. Feeling out of depth with parsers and compilers, Boshen started writing a JavaScript compiler from scratch to learn, and by March 2023 that personal project, the JavaScript Oxidation Compiler, had a linter that processed about 1,000 files in 100 milliseconds. A Rust Magazine article from then describes the work: allocating the whole syntax tree in a memory arena, shrinking source positions to 32 bits, and parsing files in parallel.

Oxlint became generally available in December 2023, pitched as a fast first pass before ESLint rather than a replacement; Shopify cut a 75-minute lint to about 10 seconds. In 2024 VoidZero, whose team includes Boshen Chen, picked Oxc over SWC as the base for Rolldown, Vite’s new bundler, and from October 2024 held Oxc’s copyright and funded its development. A transformer (2024) and minifier (2025) followed, then Oxlint 1.0 in June 2025, the Oxfmt formatter in December 2025, and stable type-aware linting in July 2026. Since June 2026 VoidZero is part of Cloudflare, and Oxc stays MIT-licensed.

choices.choice: Allocate the syntax tree in a memory arena
choices.why: An arena grabs memory in big chunks and frees it all at once, so building and dropping a tree is cheap. Boshen reported about 20% faster parsing after switching, at the cost of lifetime annotations everywhere in the Rust code.

choices.choice: Shared building blocks for every tool
choices.why: The linter, formatter, transformer, minifier and bundler all use the same parser, semantic analysis and resolver, so work isn’t duplicated and behaviour stays consistent across the stack.

choices.choice: Compatibility over a fresh rule set
choices.why: Oxlint ports ESLint rules and runs ESLint plugins, and Oxfmt matches Prettier’s output, so teams can switch without arguing about new rules or reformatting the codebase in a new style.
Rather than reimplement TypeScript’s type checker, `tsgolint` is built directly on TypeScript 7, so lint rules see exactly the types the compiler sees.

timeline.text: Boshen Chen writes about the JavaScript Oxidation Compiler, a personal project (March)
Transformer alpha; VoidZero founded to build Rolldown on Oxc
Oxfmt beta (February), JS plugins alpha (March), stable type-aware linting (July)
VoidZero joins Cloudflare (June); Oxc stays MIT-licensed
